about: The Barrow-Kin's king-barrow: a deep site generated from what it was for. They laid their first king under a mound on the bounds of their land, in a stone grave below the halls where his people were laid round him, and sealed the way down to him with a seal-stone. Levels follow the dead down: the passage-grave under the mound, the halls of the dead, the king's grave. A portal stone on a counterweight closes the stair behind the passage-grave; the king's door is sealed and the makers' warning cut round it; grave-robbers have dug their own way to the king's treasury; a light-box over the door lets in a thread of daylight and is a second way out. Roles give each room its names and its scene. Written by hand.

plan.wooded: the old dead under the beeches
plan.seen: a great long mound with a door of stone

names: a gap where the bones have fallen
the stair behind the portal stone

wooded: Standing stones make a court in the dark under the old woods. It curves in to a low door under a lintel of one stone. Whoever set them meant them to face the sunrise. The woods have grown over the mound since, and down here they face nothing.
buried: A court of standing stones in the dark under {town}, curving in to a low door under a lintel of one stone. Whoever set them meant them to face the sunrise; the town was built over them, and down here they face nothing.
scenes: A forecourt of standing stones faces the sunrise, curving in to the mound's high end. Between the two tallest is the door, a low black square under a lintel of one stone.
A passage of upright slabs runs into the mound, roofed with stones laid across, so low you go bent. The slabs are cut with spirals and with lines that might be roads.
The passage opens into a chamber shaped like a cross. Its roof rises in courses, each stone set a little further in, until one stone closes it. Basins of stone stand in the arms, with ash in them.
A recess off the chamber holds a stone basin. The burned bones of the first-laid are heaped in it, a bead or two among them.
In this recess the slabs are carved closer than anywhere else. Every one bears the same sign, a ring with a dot at its centre.

finds.cue: a bead or two among them
finds.found: Among the burned bones in the basin, a string of amber beads, the cord gone to nothing and the beads still in their order.

wooded: A slot in the stones over the door, a shaft of slabs going up into the roots of the beeches. Once it let the sun down the passage on one morning of the year. Now only a draught comes down it, smelling of leaf-mould. It is wide enough for a body to squeeze through.
buried: A slot in the stones over the door, a shaft of slabs going up into the dark under {town}. Once it let the sun down the passage on one morning of the year; now only a draught comes down it, smelling of the town. It is wide enough for a body to squeeze through.
scenes: Over the door is a slot, a box of slabs open to the sky at one end. On one morning of the year the sun comes through it down the whole passage. It is wide enough for a body to squeeze through.
Robbers have camped under the overhang of the forecourt: a hearth of three stones, a bundle of picks, a sack with the bottom cut out.
The chamber's far arm ends in a single tall stone, smooth and uncarved. Where it does not quite meet the wall, a draught comes up from below. A portal stone hangs in a slot in the rock beside it.
The stair comes down into a low hall cut in the chalk under the mound. Its white walls are grey with old lamp-smoke. Niches run away along both walls in rows.
A long hall of niches, each with its dead laid on their side, knees drawn up, a pot by the head. The floor is swept clean, though nobody living has been down here in an age.
A hall with a hearth and benches cut in the chalk, where the living sat with the dead the night before a burial. Bone flutes hang on pegs along the wall, a whole row of them, long silent.
Bones stacked in walls: skulls in rows between courses of long bones, built up to the roof like masonry. In one place the wall has fallen, and someone has dug through behind it.
A gallery runs on under the halls. Its walls are painted with people walking one way, toward its end, carrying pots, children, flutes and lights.
A room of stone tables and stone basins, where the dead were made ready. Jars stand in niches, sealed with clay and marked, and the air still smells faintly of resin.
A shaft drops away in the floor, ringed with a low kerb worn smooth by hands. Far down, something white catches your light: what was thrown in.
The gallery ends at a door of two posts and a lintel, each a single stone, carved closer than anything else here. Between them is a black opening as tall as a man.
Beyond the door the chalk gives way to old dark rock. A small chamber, empty but for a stone bench and the marks of the many who have knelt before it.
A low room of stone shelves, most of them bare now. On the floor, a rotted sack, a pick, and a man's bones lie where the robbers' tunnel comes through the wall.
A long low chamber cut before the king's grave. Stone benches run down both walls, where the king's guard were laid in their arms, and most of the benches are empty.
The grave of the first king is a hall: a ring of standing stones under the rock. In the middle of the ring is a stone bier, and on it a cloak gone to dust in the shape of a body.
Behind the ring a smooth-sided pit goes down into the rock. A smell of turned earth comes up out of it. Whatever lies at the bottom of it is not the king, or is not only the king.

incomers.label: the gnolls
incomers.role: a pack of gnolls come in from outside to dig at the dead

groups.label: the rats
groups.role: rats that live on what the mound gives up

groups.label: the bats
groups.role: bats that roost in the passage roof

groups.label: the beetles
groups.role: beetles as big as a hand, among the bones

groups.label: the dead of the mound
groups.role: the barrow's dead, risen and going nowhere

groups.label: the ghouls
groups.role: things that came down for the dead and stayed, and wait in the dark of the halls for what comes after them

groups.label: the bone hounds
groups.role: hounds of knitted bone, that keep the halls

groups.label: the restless dead
groups.role: two of the laid dead, who do not lie still

groups.label: the corpse-lights
groups.role: lights that go before the dead and lead the living astray

groups.label: the king's men
groups.role: the king's own, laid with him and risen with him

groups.label: the shades
groups.role: shades that walk the king's grave, and cool the air before them

groups.label: the drinker
groups.role: one of the king's house who would not lie down, and is thirsty

groups.label: the robbers' captain
groups.role: the captain of the grave-robbers, who means to have the king's gold

parley.ask: Ask {band} what is worth having down here
parley.tells: 'Not the king's door,' says {band}. 'There are words cut round it I would not read twice. We went under it. Behind the fallen bones in the ossuary there's a tunnel up into his treasury. Go quiet, and leave me my share.'
parley.found: Behind the fallen bones in the ossuary, a tunnel propped with grave-boards goes down under the king's door. It is the robbers' way to his treasury.
parley.slips: Taken for one of the gang, you hear the gang's business. Nobody breaks the king's door. A tunnel behind the fallen bones in the ossuary comes up in his treasury.
parley.quit: The recess is empty. The captain's fire has been kicked out and the bedroll taken; only a cut strap and the smell of smoke are left. The warning was taken.
parley.sign: No smoke comes down the passage now. The robbers' fire is out.
parley.known: The captain is waiting, sword out. A night was long enough to think over what you said you were after.

groups.label: the great hound
groups.role: the king's own hound, knitted of bones bigger than a horse's

groups.label: the mourners
groups.role: mourners who never stopped mourning, whose keening goes before them down the long halls

groups.label: the king's champions
groups.role: the champions who were laid at the king's door, and stand there still

groups.label: the king's priest
groups.role: the priest who laid the king down, and keeps his door still

groups.label: the king's horse
groups.role: the black horse they buried with the king, burning where its eyes were

keeper.label: the king under the mound
keeper.role: the first king of the Barrow-Kin, who keeps the bounds

words.Warns: The king sits up on his bier, slowly, the way a man sits up who has been called, and turns his face toward you. There is no face, only the crown. Round his bier the shields of his household lie in a ring, and every one of them is split to the boss, and the floor between them is darker than the dark. He is in no hurry. He has never needed to be.
words.Flinches: The light of day comes into the king's hall with you, and the king puts up an arm against it as the living do, and goes back from it, step by step, into the deep grave behind the ring.

keeper.robbed: The crown comes up off the king's head, and his dry hands close on the air where it was. Then he is off the bier and coming for you.

bane.seen: In one niche, behind the sealed jars, stands a jar of thick old glass stoppered with clay, and it is full of light: not lamplight, but daylight.
bane.cut: HE CANNOT ABIDE THE DAY. THE EMBALMERS KEPT THE DAY IN A JAR.
bane.fact: What sleeps in the king's grave cannot abide the light of day; the embalmers of the Barrow-Kin kept day in a jar against it.
bane.aim: Find the jar of day the embalmers kept, before you go down to the king.

objective.item: the crown of the first king
objective.text: The Barrow-Kin buried their first king with the crown they made him out of the first gold of their land, and laid his people round him to keep him. Whoever brings the crown out from under the mound has the bounds' own crown.
objective.goal: Bring the crown of the first king up out of {name}, from the king's bier.
objective.raised: In the daylight the crown of the first king, out from under {name} at last, is only a crown, a ring of soft gold, very old, and the day is the same day it was.

rumours: 'The king-barrow at {name}? The old folk's first king is under it, they say, with his crown on, and all his people round him. Robbers go in every few years. Some come out.'
'There was a man went into {name} after the king's gold and came out with a pocket of amber and his hair gone white. Grave-goods, gold, jet, amber: I buy them and I do not ask whose they were.'

land.blight: No bird sits on the mound. The grass on it grows long and pale and nothing grazes it, though the sheep crop the field round it to the stones.

signs.rites: The dead in this mound do not lie still. In the mornings the grass over the chambers is pressed flat in the shape of a large body, though no beast grazes the mound.
signs.woodcraft: Hares lie out on every field round here but this one, and the owls hunt the mound and nothing else. Whatever comes up out of it by night, the voles keep well away from.

land.healed: A blackbird is singing on the mound, and the sheep have come up onto it to graze.

trade.topic: what is buried in the king-barrow
trade.says: weighs a bead of amber on a fingertip. 'Bring me what the old folk buried and I will pay what it is worth.'
trade.shown: What you sold {merchant} out of {name} is in the glass case by the door now, on black cloth. Its price is one nobody in the town will pay.

hook.below: 'Past the first door?' says {keeper}. 'Into the halls of the old dead?' The cloth goes down on the counter. 'My mother would not walk over that ground after dark. You'll eat on the house tonight, and I'll not ask what you saw.'
hook.home: 'Out from under {name}?' {keeper} puts down the jug and looks a long while at the crown, and does not touch it. 'My grandmother said the king would keep it till the mound fell in. Tonight you eat and sleep on the house, and I will be telling this in the taproom for a year.'

camp.later: The same party camped here too, further in: the ring of stones again, a smaller fire, and less left beside it than outside, a blanket and an empty water-skin, as if they were travelling lighter by now.
camp.scene: A party camped here not long ago, in the lee of a slab: a ring of stones round dead ashes, a bedroll stiff with damp. A pack lies with its straps cut, and nobody came back for it.
journal: A notebook, swollen with damp. 'The portal stone is down and its weight is jammed in the slot. A bar under the weight would free it, Ebbe says. The light comes in through a box over the door at sunrise; we got in that way.'

A notebook, the last pages written small. 'The king's door is sealed with a stone and there are words round it nobody can read. The robbers have dug round it through the ossuary, and they did not come back. In the embalmers' room there is a jar that is warm to the touch.'
A notebook with one line in it, written by someone lying down: 'he is not asleep'.

outside: The mound lies long on the land, grassed over, higher at its east end. At the high end a forecourt of standing stones curves in to the door, and on the lintel, cut in the old script: {oldup}.
wooded: The stair ends at a door of dressed stone set in the rock, older than the woods above it. On the lintel, cut in the old script: {oldup}.
under: The stair ends at a door of dressed stone set in the rock, older than the town's cellars above it. On the lintel, cut in the old script: {oldup}.

negligible.name: a string of amber beads
negligible.text: Amber beads on a cord gone to nothing, warm-coloured even in the dark.

negligible.name: a jet button
negligible.text: A button of black jet, polished, with a hole drilled through it on the slant.

negligible.name: a bone flute
negligible.text: A flute made from the leg-bone of a crane, with four holes; the Barrow-Kin spoke with their dead through flutes like it.

minor.name: a bronze mirror
minor.text: A disc of bronze, its back cast with spirals, its face gone green: you can still see yourself in it, darkly.

minor.name: a silver arm-ring
minor.text: A ring of twisted silver made to be worn above the elbow.

minor.name: a gold cloak-pin
minor.text: A pin of gold with a head like a sun, for a cloak that rotted round it.

major.name: a gold torc
major.text: A torc of twisted gold, heavy, its ends cast as two heads looking at each other.

major.name: a jet necklace
major.text: A necklace of jet plates and beads, strung in the order they were found, black and bright.

major.name: a bronze shield-boss
major.text: The bronze boss of a shield long gone, cast with a face.

grand.name: a gold lunula
grand.text: A crescent of beaten gold, thin as a leaf, made to lie on a breast: a queen's, or a priest's.

grand.name: a gold cup
grand.text: A cup beaten out of a single piece of gold, corrugated like a shell, made for one drink.

shortcuts.unmade: A square shaft goes up through the roof of the hall, its edges worn smooth by ropes. The Barrow-Kin let their dead down this way. A bronze ring is set in the floor beneath it.
shortcuts.made: Your rope hangs down the dead-shaft, made fast to the bronze ring.
shortcuts.make: Climb the dead-shaft and leave a rope hanging in it
shortcuts.told: Your rope hangs in the dead-shaft now. From the way in, you can go straight down it to the halls.

shortcuts.unmade: Over the stone bench a narrow chimney goes up through the dark rock, cut straight and true. The smoke of the king's pyre went up this way. Iron staples climb it a little way, then stop.
shortcuts.made: Your rope hangs down the king's chimney from the topmost staple.
shortcuts.make: Climb the king's chimney and leave a rope hanging in it
shortcuts.told: Your rope hangs in the king's chimney now. From the way in, you can go straight down it to the antechamber.
shortcuts.way: the rope in the king's chimney

winch.seized: The portal stone stands down across the stair behind the back-stone, and its counterweight hangs jammed in its slot, wedged with fallen stone.
winch.turning: The counterweight runs free in its slot, and the portal stone can be raised off the stair and let down again.
winch.shut: A portal stone stands down across the stair, as heavy as a house-wall, and its counterweight will not move.
winch.climb: the gap over the portal stone

seal.thing: the seal-stone across the king's door
seal.noun: the sealed door of the king-barrow
seal.standing: A seal-stone as tall as a man closes the king's door, its edges packed with clay and the clay marked with handprints.
seal.broken: The seal-stone lies cracked across the threshold, and the king's door stands open.
seal.rebuild: Set the seal-stone back across the king's door
seal.words: the words cut round the king's door
seal.unread: Words are cut all round the king's door, in the old script, deep and close. Someone who reads the old script could say what they mean.
seal.readLabel: Read what is cut round the king's door
seal.read: {oldup}. HERE THE KING KEEPS THE BOUNDS. LET HIM KEEP THEM. {FATE}
seal.told: Read aloud, the old words say plainly enough who is behind the door, and what he cannot abide.

loosed.scene: The king's men have come up through the broken door. They stand on this side of it now, with the living.
loosed.sign: A cold comes down the stair to meet you, and the smell of the grave with it. The king's men are walking the halls.

vent.found: Where the light and the air come from: the light-box over the door, a slot of stones a body could squeeze through, out to the top of the mound.
vent.sign: A thread of grey daylight lies along the floor of the passage, coming from somewhere above the door.
vent.night: A breath of night air comes along the floor of the passage, from somewhere above the door, and it smells of grass.
vent.rungs: the climb out over the lintel

kindling.whole: On the stone tables lie the embalmers' last lengths of linen, rolled and stiff with resin, waiting for dead who never came.
kindling.burnt: The stone tables are black with soot where the resined linen burned, and the smell of it hangs in the room.
kindling.catches: The resined linen catches at once. It burns high, roll after roll, with a hard yellow light.
kindling.told: In its light the paintings on the walls show the embalmers sealing the noon sun into jars for the king's door.

warlords.scene: The warlords who came after the Barrow-Kin made a fort of the forecourt: a bank of earth thrown up across it, with a palisade's post-holes along the top, and a ditch the grass has half filled.

document.name: the words cut on the passage stone
document.shut: On one slab of the passage the warlords have cut words in the kingdom's letters, not the old script, over the spirals.
document.label: Read the words on the passage stone
document.text: HELD FOR THE LORD OF {kingdomup}. WHOEVER GOES DOWN GOES DOWN BY HIS LEAVE.

abbots.scene: The brothers who came after the Barrow-Kin hung a bell in the mourners' hall and cut their sign over the hearth, and said their own prayers for the old dead.

document.name: the brothers' tablet
document.shut: A slate tablet hangs on a peg among the bone flutes, written over in a careful hand.
document.label: Read the brothers' tablet
document.text: The brothers of {kingdom} prayed here for the dead of the old folk, and sealed the king's door a second time with a blessing. Let no one break it, and let the old king keep his bounds.

valuable.name: a brothers' hand-bell
valuable.text: A hand-bell of bronze with the brothers' sign cast on it, rung for the dead.

princes.scene: The merchant-princes after the Barrow-Kin sent men down for the king's gold: their tally of what they took is scratched on the wall, and stops after the third line.

document.name: a scratched tally
document.shut: Lines are scratched in the wall by the robbers' tunnel, in the kingdom's letters.
document.label: Read the scratched tally
document.text: For the {kingdom} company: four torcs, a cup, eleven pins of gold. The men will not go past the ring. Given up.

plague.scene: When the plague came, the town laid its own dead in the old king's recesses, wrapped in sacking, and limed them, and went away.

winter.scene: In the long winter people lived in the passage-grave, where the cold could not get in: there are hearths in the arms of the chamber, and the basins have been used to cook in.

heirs.scene: In the war of the heirs an heir's man climbed down into the well of offerings with his lord's coin to hide: there are new knots in an old rope tied to the kerb.

hidden.found: At the bottom of the well, among the offerings, a strongbox an heir's man lowered in the war of the heirs.

valuable.name: an heir's strongbox
valuable.text: An iron box with a broken seal, full of the coin of a kingdom that no longer exists.

raiders.scene: Raiders from over the sea dug into the forecourt one summer looking for gold, and gave up: there is a trench half across it, and a broken spade in the bottom.

marks.name: the marks on the kerb-stones
marks.unread: Marks run along the kerb-stones of the forecourt in the old script.
marks.read: The marks are the makers' own, cut when the mound was raised: who lies within, and what they were.
marks.label: Read the marks on the kerb-stones

cache.cue: At the far end of the hall the niches stop. The wall there is of smaller stones, laid dry and close, with none of the dead in it.
cache.searched: The small stones at the end of the hall are not the barrow's. They are laid against an opening, and a cold draught comes between them.
cache.found: At the end of the hall of the bones, a later wall of small stones closes a chamber off.
cache.mark: the mark on the small stones
cache.markseen: A mark is scratched into one of the small stones: a word in the kingdom's letters, and under it a tally.
cache.readlabel: Make out the mark scratched in the small stones
cache.lore: It is the kingdom's script, in a hurried hand: KEPT FOR THE RETURN. Under it is a tally of what was kept. The stones beneath are loose to the hand.
cache.loreno: The letters are worn past reading.
cache.forcelabel: Lever the small stones out of the wall, one by one
cache.force: It takes the best part of an hour. Every stone that comes out rings on the floor, and the sound goes down the hall. Behind them is a low chamber.
cache.chamber: A low chamber, dry, its floor swept. Along one wall, things have been set out in a row to be counted.
cache.way: the gap in the small stones
cache.docname: a folded paper under a stone
cache.docshut: A folded paper lies under a flat stone, the stone set on it to keep it.
cache.doclabel: Unfold the paper and read it
cache.doctext: In the letters of {kingdom}: 'This was taken out of the king's hall below when the seal was set again. It is kept for whoever comes back for it. Whoever comes back: the dead are not ours to keep.' No one came back.

order.chest: a stone chest with three carved bosses
order.chestseen: A stone chest stands against the wall, its lid one piece with it. Three bosses are carved along its front: {a}, {b} and {c}. Each gives a little under the thumb.
order.chestopen: The stone chest stands open, its lid turned back on a pivot.
order.friezeseen: A frieze is painted along the wall: the dead carried to their barrow. First, leading the bearers, goes {first}. Among them walks {second}. Last comes {third}.
order.known: The frieze in the halls shows the order of the procession: {first}, then {second}, then {third}.
order.held: The boss sinks under your thumb and stays down.
order.wrong: The boss sinks, and every boss springs back up with a crack that goes down the halls.
order.right: The last boss sinks. A catch turns over inside the chest, and the lid swings up on its pivot.
order.readlabel: Read the makers' marks on the chest
order.lore: Under each boss is a count in the makers' letters. In that count: {first}, then {second}, then {third}.
order.loreno: The marks under the bosses are worn. You cannot make the count out.
order.forcelabel: Break the chest's lid off by main force
order.force: It takes an hour, and the lid comes off in two pieces. What the chest held is crushed under it.
